settings.text: One wheel, one kiln.Two firings a year.
We do not make to order and we do not repeat a firing. What leaves here is what one potter and two apprentices can throw, glaze and fire properly in six months, which is about forty pieces a kiln.
Tiradentes, and a kiln in the yard.
Teresa has thrown here for nineteen years. The apprentices stay three years each and take the wheel for the second firing of every year — those pieces carry their mark, not hers.

settings.image_alt: The wheel and the kiln yard in Tiradentes

settings.heading: Dug in Minas, blended here
settings.text: Two stoneware bodies from the same pit outside São Thomé, blended wet in the yard and rested a month before anything is thrown.

settings.heading: Forty pieces, one pair of hands
settings.text: Thrown on the wheel and turned by hand at the leather-hard stage. The foot is where the number is cut, and it is cut before the glaze goes on.

settings.heading: Four glazes, mixed by weight
settings.text: Ash, oatmeal, iron and a clear. All four are mixed here from raw materials, and the recipes are published in the journal.

settings.heading: Thirty-six hours of wood
settings.text: Stoked in pairs, day and night, to 1,280°C. What the flame does to a glaze on one side of the kiln it will not do on the other, and that is the last ten per cent we do not control.

settings.image_alt: A pot being turned on the wheel at the leather-hard stage
settings.heading: How a piece is made
Breakages, first year
settings.text: Replaced from the next firing, free. Photograph it and write; we do not ask you to post the pieces back.

settings.heading: Completing a set
settings.text: Give us the number cut into the foot and we match the glaze as closely as a wood kiln allows — and say honestly how close that is.

settings.heading: Repairs in gold
settings.text: Quoted first. A clean break can be joined with gold rather than hidden, which is the older and better answer.
